hypotheses.title: Pure Long-Horizon Option Net Breakeven Asymmetry (Zero Price Overlays)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: In the options market (option9), institutional investors express long-term directional bias and tail-risk hedging through open-interest weighted breakeven pricing. The compact net breakeven asymmetry term ((call_breakeven_180 + put_breakeven_180 - 2 * close) / close) measures the net upside vs downside breakeven price distance. Using pure option geometry without any equity price or VWAP overlays and standardizing via rolling 60-day z-scores produces an unpolluted institutional positioning signal with balanced turnover and high risk-adjusted Sharpe across TOP3000.
confounders: Unscheduled corporate acquisitions where deep in-the-money options distort open-interest breakeven distributions
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if pure 180-day breakeven asymmetry achieves Sharpe < 1.30 or Fitness < 1.00 in TOP3000.

candidates.rationale: Pure 180-day net breakeven asymmetry standardized over 60 days, subindustry-neutralized and uniformly ranked without price overlays.

hypotheses.title: Options Put-Call Open Interest Term Dislocation Sentiment Reversal
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Put-to-call open interest ratios (option9) reflect aggregate market hedging demand. Comparing the 90-day baseline put-call ratio (pcr_oi_90) against the near-term 30-day ratio (pcr_oi_30) captures short-term sentiment dislocations. When pcr_oi_90 exceeds pcr_oi_30, near-term hedging panic has dissipated while long-term institutional call positioning remains intact, creating a bullish sentiment unwinding drift across TOP3000.
confounders: Index option market-wide hedging flows that distort single-stock equity option open interest ratios
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if put-call OI term dislocation fails to achieve Sharpe >= 1.25 in TOP3000.

candidates.rationale: Subindustry-standardized 60-day z-score of 90d versus 30d put-call open interest ratio spread.

hypotheses.title: Synthetic Forward Price Implied Basis Momentum
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Synthetic forward prices (forward_price_60) derived from at-the-money options via put-call parity encode the market maker's implied cost-of-carry and share borrowing costs. When the synthetic forward trades at an expanding premium over cash equity ((forward_price_60 - close) / close), options market makers are demanding a premium to borrow shares, reflecting acute institutional demand to establish long forward exposure.
confounders: Unscheduled ex-dividend dates or special cash dividends that mechanically depress synthetic forward pricing
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if synthetic forward basis momentum yields Sharpe < 1.25 or fails sub-universe consistency in TOP3000.

candidates.rationale: Subindustry-neutralized 60-day z-score of synthetic 60-day forward price premium over cash equity.
